memoryRss.description: Resident Set Size (RSS) memory consumption measured across idle state, sustained produce workload (50k msg/s), and multi-consumer fanout.
memoryRss.keyInsight: Krabka operates in a fraction of the memory because it avoids JVM object header bloat, uses zero-copy byte buffers with Tokio, and avoids speculative GC buffer reservations.

startupTime.description: Elapsed time from Kubernetes pod launch until the broker joins the KRaft quorum and acknowledges its first produce request.
startupTime.keyInsight: Native Rust compilation and immediate KRaft log recovery allow Krabka pods to reach Ready state and serve traffic in ~1.2 seconds without JVM classloading or JIT warm-up.

throughputPerCore.description: Sustained produce message throughput per available vCPU core under saturated 100-byte message workload (acks=all).
throughputPerCore.keyInsight: Direct I/O and asynchronous vectored write pipelines maximize IOPS and network saturation per core.

tailLatencyP99.description: 99th-percentile producer acknowledgement latency under a constant 50,000 msg/sec rate without coordinated omission.
tailLatencyP99.keyInsight: Deterministic memory management eliminates JVM garbage collection pauses (Stop-The-World events) that cause tail latency spikes.
